name: TokuMX
tagline: MongoDB 2.4 fork on fractal-tree indexes with compression and transactions; EOL since 2017.
description: TokuMX was Tokutek's fork of MongoDB 2.4 that swapped the storage layer for fractal tree indexes. Compared with MongoDB of that era it offered document-level concurrency instead of a database-wide lock, compression of all data by default, MVCC with multi-statement transactions on a single server, and no fragmentation, while keeping MongoDB's drivers, replication and sharding. It lacked text and geospatial indexes. Percona acquired it with Tokutek in 2015, made its last release in September 2015 and ended support on May 1, 2017, recommending Percona Server for MongoDB instead.
statusNote: Percona's last TokuMX release was Sept 2015 and support ended May 1, 2017; Percona recommends migrating to Percona Server for MongoDB.

pricing.notes: Community edition was free; an enterprise edition with hot backup was sold until EOL.

scale.notes: Inherited MongoDB 2.4 replica sets and sharding.

strengths: Document-level locking at a time when MongoDB locked whole databases
Default compression cut storage dramatically for large collections
Single-node multi-statement transactions with MVCC snapshots
Drop-in for MongoDB 2.4 drivers and tooling
weaknesses: Frozen at MongoDB 2.4 semantics; no modern drivers or features
No text search or geospatial indexes
End of life since 2017 with no security fixes
useCases: Historical reference for write-optimised MongoDB storage
